I reviewed all of lines 1–186 against the repeated-proof-machinery rubric. I did not search other files, so I did not check whether an existing Mathlib lemma already covers the shared step below.

The only repeated non-boilerplate step is the estimate ‖ℓ x‖ₑ ≤ ‖x‖ₑ for ‖ℓ‖ₑ ≤ 1. It appears as `(ContinuousLinearMap.le_opENorm _ _).trans (mul_le_of_le_one_left (by positivity) hℓ)` in `semivariation_le_variation` and in `exists_subset_lt_enorm_apply_of_lt_semivariation`. It is a one-line term that combines two existing lemmas. A helper would save very little, and the rubric treats short calculations and thin wrappers as insufficient.

The openings of `semivariation_union_le`, `semivariation_mono` and `semivariation_le_variation` (`simp only [semivariation, iSup_le_iff]; intro ℓ hℓ`) are routine unfolding. The repeated `μ.mapRange (ℓ : E →+ ℝ) ℓ.continuous` expression is notation noise, not repeated reasoning. The `μ t = μ s - μ (s \ t)` computation and the `hs`, `hu` and `s_anti` steps each occur once. Nothing else is duplicated across proofs.
